title: Dedicated Instance
blurb: The private Unified CM add-on: what Cisco deploys, how activation sizes it, and how you reach it from Control Hub.

lessons.title: What Cisco deploys
lessons.summary: Dedicated Instance is an add-on to Webex Calling. Cisco deploys Unified CM, Unity Connection, and Expressway. IM and Presence and Emergency Responder are not in every sentence of the docs.
objectives: State when IM and Presence is included

diagram.caption: Activation deploys the UC applications. The access article lists what you can cross-launch.

steps.label: Activate the add-on
steps.detail: Dedicated Instance is purchased before activation. You can activate in the First-Time Setup Wizard or later.
steps.inspect: Calling > Dedicated Instance > Status

steps.label: Deploy the core apps
steps.detail: Unified CM, Unity Connection, and Expressway-Core and Edge are deployed and sized from the counts you enter.
steps.inspect: Per region

steps.label: Choose Legacy Jabber or not
steps.detail: IM and Presence is no longer deployed by default. It is deployed only if you selected Legacy Jabber for calling, messaging, and presence.
steps.inspect: Do not assume Jabber

steps.label: Notice the region words
steps.detail: The activation article says Emergency Responder only in the AMER region. The deployment-models introduction says CER for U.S. customers, and a later paragraph says North American customers.
steps.inspect: Quote the page you are using

paragraphs: As part of service activation, Cisco deploys and sizes Unified CM, Unity Connection, Expressway-Core and Edge, and Emergency Responder only in the AMER region.

Cisco Unified IM and Presence is deployed only when the First-Time Setup Wizard option for Legacy Jabber is selected. The access article still lists IM and Presence and optional Session Management Edition among the applications you can cross-launch when they exist.

Activation: only in the AMER region. Access from Control Hub: only for AMER. The deployment-models introduction says U.S. customers, and the activation paragraph on that same page says North American customers.
This lab does not pick a winner. When you design a region, read the page that matches the task and ask Cisco if the wording still conflicts.

lessons.title: Size it in the wizard
lessons.summary: Professional, Standard, and Workspace counts size the region. They are not a second license pool. The voice service domain is capped and then locked.
objectives: Enter device counts that fit the subscription
Keep the voice service domain within ten characters
Know that a region activation is not reversible

diagram.caption: Counts size the cluster. The subscription still owns the licenses.

flow.title: Activate a region without painting yourself in

steps.label: Use the welcome email
steps.detail: The provisioning contact gets the email. The partner administrator email in the wizard is mandatory and receives UC access details.
steps.inspect: Same email must sign in to the Webex App

steps.label: Enter counts
steps.detail: Specify Professional, Standard, and Workspace devices per region. The sum across regions cannot exceed the subscription.
steps.inspect: Standard appears only if it was ordered

steps.label: Check ten characters
steps.detail: The voice service domain becomes editable after a region is selected. It is filled from the SIP address and must not exceed ten characters.
steps.inspect: It applies to UC apps and MRA

steps.label: Lock the choice
steps.detail: Once a region is activated it cannot be reversed or moved. There are no new Dedicated Instance deployments in EMEA; choose EU or UK.
steps.inspect: Later regions reuse the same voice domain

paragraphs: The parameters size the Dedicated Instance UC applications for that region. Cisco's deployment-models page says Cisco is responsible for cluster sizing based on the licenses purchased and the First Time Setup Wizard input.
Do not treat the wizard counts as extra licenses. They have to fit inside the Webex Calling subscription.
The voice service domain used for the first region applies to later regions in the same organization. The UC applications domain cannot be modified after the service is submitted or activated.
Skipping regions is allowed: leave them unselected and finish later from Calling > Dedicated Instance > Status.

lessons.title: Cross-launch and Web RTMT
lessons.summary: Calling, Dedicated Instance, Manage opens the UC applications. Web RTMT is limited to specific administrator roles, and it is view-oriented.
objectives: Name who can open Web RTMT
Know the cookie and SSO limits

diagram.caption: Control Hub is the door. The UC portal is still the UC portal.

flow.title: Open Unified CM without a VPN

steps.label: Services > Calling > Dedicated Instance > Manage
steps.detail: Select the UC application and click Manage. The built-in portal opens in a new tab. The browser must allow cookies.
steps.inspect: Supported: Firefox, Chrome, Edge, Safari

steps.label: Local admin login
steps.detail: For SSO-enabled UC applications the recovery URL opens. SSO itself cannot be configured through cross-launch.
steps.inspect: Configure SSO on the application page

steps.label: Launch from the publisher
steps.detail: Partner Sales Full Administrator, or a customer Full Administrator or Read-only Administrator. Allow cookies for https://apps.ucmgmt.cisco.com.
steps.inspect: Subscriber logs are chosen after launch

steps.label: Do not expect a WebRTMT email group
steps.detail: Configuring an email group for WebRTMT alerts is not supported in Dedicated Instance. Use a Control Hub delivery channel.
steps.inspect: Metrics on the overview are view only

paragraphs: Version, server FQDN, internal IP, publisher or subscriber role, activated services, datacenter, voice service domain, and the Expressway Edge public IP.
Application changes sync to Control Hub on a 24-hour schedule. A change you just made may not be on that pane yet.
Web RTMT monitors Unified CM, IM and Presence, and Unity Connection for the roles named above. The cross-launch is over the top and does not require VPN.
Replication states you can read there include INIT, INCORRECT, GOOD, SUSPECT, and FAILED. INIT lasting more than an hour may mean setup failed.

sections.h: Why a forwarder instead of a local zone
paragraphs: Cisco hosts the records. Your DNS only has to send queries for that suffix to Cisco's Dedicated Instance DNS.
If the forwarder is missing, on-premises devices cannot resolve the service name even when the WAN is up.
The same article describes Edge Connect at Equinix or Megaport, with peering at two sites in a region. Over-the-top still exists for cross-launch.
This lab does not invent circuit IDs or POP lists beyond those two providers.

lessons.title: Directory sync wants SSO
lessons.summary: End users sync to Control Hub, then Dedicated Instance Unified CM syncs from Control Hub. That path requires single sign-on. Native Unified CM user options remain.
objectives: Name the fallback the article allows

steps.detail: Dedicated Instance Unified CM then synchronizes from Control Hub.
steps.inspect: Not the other way as the primary story

steps.label: Turn it on or lose the feature
steps.detail: User synchronization functions only when SSO is enabled. Without SSO, directory synchronization is not supported.
steps.inspect: Do not promise sync without it

sections.h: One sentence you can say in a design review
paragraphs: Directory sync from Control Hub into Dedicated Instance requires SSO. Without SSO the feature is not supported, and native Unified CM user options still exist.
Control Hub directory synchronization is shared across Meetings, Webex Calling, and Dedicated Instance.
It is not a statement that every Dedicated Instance feature requires SSO. Cross-launch of an SSO-enabled UC app uses the recovery URL and local admin credentials.
It is not a promise about contact-center agent sync. That is a different service.

paragraphs: PSTN calls in that example leave Dedicated Instance through multi-tenant Webex Calling to a Cloud Connected PSTN provider. MRA users are included in that aggregate.
